title: SRE in 30 days
summary: Telemetry first, then service level objectives, incidents, on-call and capacity, with a widget or practice task every day.
who: Engineers who run production systems, or want to, and are comfortable on a Linux server.
outcomes: Instrument a service and read its metrics, logs and traces.
Set an SLO, work out the error budget and explain burn rate to your team.
Run an incident, write a blameless postmortem and design on-call that people can sustain.

days.title: Practice and review: telemetry and alerts

items.text: Run the trade-off calculators for error budgets and redundancy

title: System design in 30 days
summary: From estimation and caching to quorums, cells and worked designs, with the lab and mock interview on the practice days.
who: Engineers who already operate services and want to design them, or prepare for design interviews.
outcomes: Estimate load and storage, then pick the right building blocks.
Reason about consistency, failure domains and blast radius.
Walk through a worked design in an interview, with trade-offs.

days.title: Practice: estimate and break a design
Practice: fail a design on purpose

items.text: Break a design against its error budget
Run a timed mock design interview

title: Kubernetes operator in 30 days
summary: Workloads, networking, storage and security, then upgrades, etcd, RBAC and cluster debugging.
who: Engineers who can use containers and want to run clusters in production.
outcomes: Deploy, scale and debug workloads with the right probes and resources.
Explain how traffic, storage and policy work inside a cluster.
Back up etcd, upgrade a cluster safely and handle a node loss.

title: Linux and shell in 30 days
summary: Files, users, processes, disks, services and troubleshooting, then the shell scripting to automate them.
who: People starting out in DevOps, or developers who want to be at ease on a server.
outcomes: Work confidently on a Linux server, from permissions to systemd to performance triage.
Find out why a server is slow, full or unreachable.
Write safe shell scripts that check their own work.

title: Cloud and infrastructure as code in 30 days
summary: Cloud building blocks, access control and Terraform, from first resources to drift and state.
who: Engineers who know the basics and want to build and secure cloud infrastructure as code.
outcomes: Design a network, compute and storage layout across availability zones.
Write least-privilege access and keep secrets out of code and state.
Manage Terraform state, modules and drift on a team.

items.text: Run the cost and redundancy calculators

title: DevOps foundations: the 100-day challenge
summary: One lesson a day for 100 days, from Linux and the shell to networking, containers and pipelines, with a review day each week. Free, offline, and your progress stays on your device.
who: Anyone who wants a steady daily habit to move into DevOps, or to fill gaps in the basics.
outcomes: Work confidently on a Linux server from the command line and automate with Bash and Python.
Use version control and explain how networks, DNS and TLS fit together.
Build and run containers, and design a pipeline that tests and ships code.
Keep a daily learning streak and finish with a portfolio of what you completed.

title: Site reliability engineering: the 100-day challenge
summary: One lesson a day for 100 days, from Linux and networking to Kubernetes, observability, SLOs, incident response and capacity, with a review day each week. Free, offline, and your progress stays on your device.
who: Engineers who want a steady daily habit to move into SRE or platform work, or to fill gaps before an on-call rotation.
outcomes: Debug a Linux server and a Kubernetes cluster from the command line.
Instrument services, write alerts that matter and read dashboards under pressure.
Define service level objectives, run an incident and write a blameless post-mortem.
Keep a daily learning streak and finish with a record of what you completed.
